title: Choose the new world for PostForge
question: Re-roll: layout is fixed — left sidebar with its current behavior, routes stay put. You are choosing the world that skins it. The roll assigned The Exhibition Wall.

options.label: The Exhibition Wall
options.thesis: Generated media hangs as works with museum wall labels; the red dot means published; ops live in the registrar's ledger grammar.
options.viewport: Home as the current exhibition: this week's works hung with wall labels and red dots, a registrar strip below carrying jobs, spend, and the outgoing-loan schedule. Sidebar unchanged in place, re-read as the room directory.
options.risk: Galleries resist density; queues, costs, and statuses must speak registrar (accession ledger, condition report) or the surface goes precious and the ops get lost.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Quantities are the interface: every metric owns a bank of glowing tube digits; a count change is a visible shift of physical depth.
options.viewport: Home as the counter wall: glowing tube banks for jobs, spend, and posts across the top, engraved labels beneath each bank, amber overflow events, media lists below on steel.
options.risk: Wins hearts instantly and then starves the product: tubes display quantities only, and PostForge's center is media, not numbers.
options.case: Wins audience identification; loses product clarity — a media-first tool cannot live inside digit banks.

options.label: Man-Machine
options.thesis: The pipeline drawn as a wiring diagram on a strict traffic grid: signal red, amber, and green on black and paper white, connectors lighting with current.
options.viewport: Home as the schematic: generation, review, automation, and publishing as wired nodes on the grid, lines carrying current to whichever stage is live, media staged in paper-white frames.
options.risk: The finest pipeline grammar in the hand, but flat signal colors compete with your actual outputs — in a media product the work must be the color.
options.case: Wins the automation and pipeline surfaces; loses media review, where enamel red fights the artwork.

options.label: Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Every zone wears its literal name in straight quotes; hazard diagonals structure the surface; the active item keeps its orange zip-tie tag on.
options.viewport: Home as the stockroom wall: "PIPELINE", "SPEND", "REVIEW" label plates set square on the grid, the day's queue under a hazard stripe, published pieces tagged orange.
options.risk: Highest cultural currency for a TikTok-marketing tool, and the shortest half-life: irony labeling in a daily-ops surface can read as gimmick within weeks.
options.case: Wins cultural resonance with the audience's content scene; loses longevity and morning-scan seriousness.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The calm grey dashboard every dev tool ships: sidebar, stat cards, one indigo accent — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Your existing sidebar and routes exactly as they are, reskinned in quiet greys with tidy stat cards; nothing surprises, nothing offends.
canonCard.risk: Interchangeable with every other self-hosted tool; safe by construction, memorable never.
